BURHAN:v3p194/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.claim: The narrative omits that the messenger took and delivered the letter; the Queen's response shows that intervening action.
BURHAN:v3p194/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ﴾ 1 الآية فأعقب بقوله حكاية عنها ﴿ قالت يا أيها الملأ إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p103/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r4.claim: In ثم تول عنهم فانظر, the intended sequence is look first and withdraw afterward; the clause order is inverted.
ITQAN:v3p103/r4.anchor: أو قلب عطف نحو ﴿ ثم تول عنهم فانظر ﴾ أي فانظر ثم تول

ELMALILI:27:21-31/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r12.claim: The Hoopoe served as a messenger carrying a letter, with the added task of withdrawing and observing the recipients’ response, beyond a pigeon simply delivering a note.
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r12.anchor: Burada hüdhüd bir posta hizmetinde kullanılmış oluyor. Fakat bunda bir güvercinin mektup götürmesinden fazla bir şey var.

ELMALILI:27:21-31/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r13.claim: Elmalılı renders the address as the country’s notables, meaning the council of people who decide its affairs.
ELMALILI:27:21-31/r13.anchor: Bunu burada “a‘yân-ı memleket” diye terceme ediyorum, çünkü:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.claim: To verify the hoopoe's report, Solomon sent a letter with it to the queen and instructed it to return with her response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:27:17/r14.anchor: yazdığı bir mektubu kraliçeye götürüp sonuçtan kendisini haberdar etmesini hüdhüde emretti.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r1.claim: Solomon already had Sabā in mind, and the lapwing may have flown there for that reason; without prior plans, a letter merely testing the bird’s truthfulness seems improbable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r1.anchor: In the absence of any prior plans, it is

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r2.claim: The letter is an ultimatum, as later verses make clear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r2.anchor: The nature of this letter is th at of an ultimatum, as will

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r3.claim: Solomon told the lapwing to withdraw after delivery and wait to observe the response.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r3.anchor: Solomon (sws) asked the lapwing to withdraw from there and wait

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r4.speaker: some scholars
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r4.claim: They say the lapwing was withdrawn so courtiers could converse freely without hesitation before a foreign envoy; Islahi rejects this because nothing indicates Sabā thought birds understood their conversation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p480/r4.anchor: Some scholars think that this directive of Solomon (sws) to withdraw from the royal court while waiting was given to the lapwing

BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r1.claim: The ب in 'go with my letter' is causative; Solomon chose the hoopoe over powerful jinn because he saw signs of knowledge, wisdom, and sound judgment in it, leaving the queen no excuse.
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r1.anchor: فتكون الباء للتعدية وتخصيصه بالرسالة دون سائر ما تحت ملكه من أبناء الجن الأقوياء على التصرف والتعرف لما عاين فيه من علامات العلم والحكمة وصحة الفراسة

BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r2.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says the hoopoe was truthful in its report, sincere in counsel to its king, and attentive to the truth, so it was rewarded with the message despite its weak outward form.
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أنه لما صدق فيما أخبر وبذل النصح لملكه

BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r3.claim: The letter is to Bilqīs and her people, since the earlier wording mentions her and her people.
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r3.anchor: {فألقه إليهم} أي : اطرحه على بلقيس وقومها لأنه ذكرهم معها

BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r4.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r4.claim: Al-Irshād explains the plural pronoun because the noble letter's message calls everyone to Islam.
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r4.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" : وجمع الضمير لما أن مضمون الكتاب الكريم دعوة الكل إلى الإسلام

BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r5.claim: The command ألقه with a silent hā is a valid pronunciation easing or a pause form; its underlying form has the object pronoun referring to the letter and is jussive for that reason.
BURSEVI:v6p248#3/r5.anchor: قوله : ألقه بسكون الهاء تخفيفا لغة صحيحة أو على نية الوقف

BURSEVI:v6p249/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r1.claim: Solomon tells the hoopoe to withdraw from the queen's company, hide nearby, and listen to the reply.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r1.anchor: أعرض عنهم بترك وليهم وقربهم وتبعد إلى مكان تتوارى فيه وتسمع ما يجيبونه

BURSEVI:v6p249/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r2.claim: The command to look means to reflect and find out.

BURSEVI:v6p249/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r3.claim: The reply in question is what the people say back and forth to one another.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r3.anchor: أي ماذا يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض من القول

BURSEVI:v6p249/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r4.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v6p249/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh parses ماذا either as an interrogative noun governed by يرجعون, or as مبتدأ plus ذا بمعنى الذي, with a deleted relative pronoun object.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r4.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : ماذا اسم واحد استفهام منصوب بيرجعون أو مبتدأ وذا بمعنى الذي

BURSEVI:v6p249/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r5.claim: A report says the hoopoe found Bilqis asleep in her palace at Ma'rib, with doors locked and keys beneath her head.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r5.anchor: روي : أن الهدهد أخذ الكتاب وأتى بلقيس فوجدها راقدة في قصرها بمأرب

BURSEVI:v6p249/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r6.claim: The hoopoe entered through an opening, dropped the letter on Bilqis's chest, withdrew, and startled her awake.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r6.anchor: فدخل من كوة وألقى الكتاب على نحرها وهي مستلقية وتأخر يسيرا فانتبهت فزعة

BURSEVI:v6p249/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r7.claim: Bilqis could read and write Arabic and descended from Tubba al-Himyari.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r7.anchor: وكانت قارئة كاتبة عربية من نسل تبع الحميري

BURSEVI:v6p249/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p249/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p249/r8.claim: Seeing the seal made Bilqis tremble and submit; she judged Solomon the greater king because birds obeyed him and his seal looked imposing.
BURSEVI:v6p249/r8.anchor: فلما رأت الخاتم ارتعدت وخضعت لأن ملك سليمان كان في خاتمه

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r1.claim: These readers connect the hāʾ to a following yāʾ in alqihī, with Ibn Dhakwān using kasra on the hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي: (فألقهى إليهم) موصولة بياء في رواية الحلواني عن هشام بن عمار عن ابن عامر

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r2.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r2.claim: Nafiʿ’s transmitters differ: several of Qālūn’s transmitters use kasra without yāʾ, while Warsh, Ismāʿīl, and al-Ḥalwānī connect a yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r2.anchor: واختلف عن نافع فقال ابن جماز والمسيبي والقاضي عن قالون: (فألقه إليهم) مكسورة الهاء من غير ياء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr has reports with a quiescent hāʾ from al-Yazīdī and a connected yāʾ from ʿAbd al-Wārith and Shujāʿ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r3.anchor: واختلف عن أبي عمرو، فروى عنه اليزيدي: فألقه ساكنة، وروى عنه عبد الوارث وشجاع، (فألقهي) موصولة بياء في الوصل.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r4.speaker: عباس وعاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r4.claim: ʿAbbās reports the sukun form as preferred but permits the yāʾ form; ʿĀṣim in both transmissions and Ḥamza use sukun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في الروايتين جميعا جزما وحمزة مثله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r5.claim: Connecting the hāʾ with yāʾ is more regular and fitting; omitting the yāʾ is mainly poetic, and the connected report from Abū ʿAmr is more regular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: وصل الهاء بياء في (ألقه) ونحوه أقيس وأشبه، وترك وصله بالياء إنما يجري في الشعر

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r6.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan calls alqih and lahu arqān dialect forms; Abū ʿAlī says Sībawayh did not record that dialect and treats the poetic example as necessity.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p386/r6.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن أن نحو: (ألقه) ونحو قوله : مشتاقان له أرقان لغة، ولم يحك ذلك سيبويه

QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#1/r1.claim: The Seven include a form with kasra on the hāʾ connection vowel instead of sukūn.
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#1/r1.anchor: Kasra on hāʾ pronoun (connection vowel) instead of sukūn; standard variant among the Seven

QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#2/r1.claim: The hāʾ suffix may be followed by long ī, extending the pronoun vowel for recitational rhythm.
QIRAAT-ER:27:28:6#2/r1.anchor: extended vowel on pronoun suffix; elongation for rhythmic/recitational purposes

QASHANI:27:28-31/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:28-31/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:28-31/r1.claim: Solomon's book signifies practical wisdom and divine law.

QASHANI:27:28-31/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:27:28-31/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:27:28-31/r2.claim: Solomon's instruction to withdraw and observe asks whether the recipients will accept obedience and submission or refuse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r5.claim: The narrative omits Solomon's order to write the letter and send the hoopoe as its messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r5.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره: فأمر بكتابة كتاب إليهم، وبذهاب الهدهد رسولا إليهم بالكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r6.claim: كتابي هذا means the letter present and written at that moment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r7.claim: Telling the hoopoe to withdraw means move nearby so it can hear their replies to one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r7.anchor: أي تنح عنهم إلى مكان قريب، بحيث تسمع ما يصدر منهم وما يرجع به بعضهم إلى بعض من القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r8.claim: The verse supports a ruler sending letters to polytheists to convey the call and invite them to Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r8.anchor: دليل على إرسال الكتب إلى المشركين من الإمام، يبلغهم الدعوة ويدعوهم إلى الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r9.claim: The Prophet wrote to Khosrow, Caesar, and other Arab kings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r9.anchor: وقد كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى كسرى وقيصر وغيرهما ملوك العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r10.speaker: وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r10.claim: Wahb says withdrawing is courtly etiquette: the hoopoe should step away as kings' manners require but remain near enough to hear the consultation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r10.anchor: وقال وهب: أمره بالتولي حسن أدب ليتنحى حسب ما يتأدب به الملوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets تول عنهم as return to Solomon after delivering the letter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أمره بالتولي بمعنى الرجوع إليه، أي ألقه وارجع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd takes فانظر ماذا يرجعون as preceding ثم تول عنهم in narrative order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r12.anchor: وقوله: فانظر ماذا يرجعون في معنى التقديم على قوله: ثم تول عنهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r13.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r13.claim: Abu Ali also proposes advancing فانظر before ثم تول عنهم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r13.anchor: وقاله أبو علي، ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى التقديم والتأخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r14.claim: The apparent sequence needs no rearrangement: observation follows the hoopoe's withdrawal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r14.anchor: بل الظاهر أن النظر معتقب التولي عنهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r15.claim: The seven readers read فألقه with a kasra and following yā, with a shortened kasra, or with a silent hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r15.anchor: وقرىء في السبعة: فألقه، بكسر الهاء وياء بعدها، وباختلاس الكسرة وبسكون الهاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r16.speaker: مسلم بن جندب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r16.claim: Muslim ibn Jundub reads فألقه with ḍamma on the hāʾ followed by wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r16.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن جندب: بضم الهاء وواو بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r17.claim: The plural إليهم refers to the hoopoe's report that it found Bilqis and her people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r17.anchor: وجمع في قوله: إليهم الهدهد قال: وجدتها وقومها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r19.claim: فانظر ماذا يرجعون can mean to consider the matter and hold it in mind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p232/r19.anchor: ومعنى: فانظر ماذا يرجعون: أي تأمل واستحضره في ذهنك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r1.claim: If نظر means reflective thought, it is suspended; ماذا may be an interrogative object, or ما may be interrogative with ذا as a relative pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r1.anchor: إن كان معنى فانظر معنى التأمل بالفكر، كان انظر معلقا، وماذا: إما كلمة استفهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r2.claim: On the interrogative parse, يرجعون predicates ماذا; on the relative parse, ذا is the predicate and يرجعون its relative clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r2.anchor: فعلى الأول يكون يرجعون خبرا عن ماذا، وعلى الثاني يكون ذا هو الخبر ويرجعون صلة ذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r3.claim: If نظر means wait, it is not a verb of cognition and does not suspend the clause; ماذا is wholly relative, meaning wait for what they say to return to me.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r3.anchor: وإن كان معنى فانظر: فانتظر، فليس فعل قلب فيعلق، بل يكون ماذا كله موصولا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r4.claim: The story omits the hoopoe taking the letter to Bilqis and her people as Solomon commanded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r4.anchor: في الكلام حذف تقديره: فأخذ الهدهد الكتاب وذهب به إلى بلقيس وقومها وألقاه إليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r5.claim: One account says the hoopoe carried the letter in its beak.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r6.claim: Another account says it hung the letter around its neck, landed over Bilqis among her troops, then dropped it in her lap after she looked up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r6.anchor: وقيل: علقه في عنقه، فجاءها حتى وقف على رأسها، وحولها جنودها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r7.claim: A report says Bilqis was asleep in her palace with its doors shut, and the hoopoe dropped the letter on her chest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r7.anchor: وقيل: كانت في قصرها قد غلقت الأبواب واستلقت على فراشها نائمة، فألقى الكتاب على نحرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r8.claim: Another account says the hoopoe blocked the sun through the window where Bilqis worshipped daily, prompting her to rise and receive the letter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r8.anchor: فجاء الهدهد فسدها بجناحه، فرأت ذلك وقامت إليه، فألقى الكتاب إليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r9.claim: A report says Bilqis was a literate Arab descended from the people of Tubbaʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r9.anchor: وكانت قارئة عربية من قوم تبع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r10.claim: Another account says the hoopoe dropped the letter through a window and concealed itself there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p233/r10.anchor: وقيل: ألقاه من كوة وتوارى فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r1.claim: The command resumes the promised inspection by explaining what Solomon ordered after writing the letter; هذا points to the present letter.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r1.anchor: استئناف مبين لكيفية النظر الذي وعده عليه السلام بعد ما كتب كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r2.claim: Solomon chose the hoopoe over other capable jinn stewards because he had seen its signs of knowledge and wisdom, leaving the recipients no excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r2.anchor: وتخصيصه عليه السلام إياه بالرسالة دون سائر ما تحت ملكه من أمناء الجن

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r3.claim: The verse supports a ruler sending letters to polytheists to convey Islam; the Prophet wrote to Khosrow, Caesar, and other Arab rulers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r3.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على جواز إرسال الكتب إلى المشركين من الامام لابلاغ الدعوة والدعاء إلى الاسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r4.speaker: السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r4.claim: The Seven readers have three forms for فألقه: kasra with a following yā, shortened kasra, and a still هاء.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r4.anchor: وقرىء السبعة فألقهبكسر الهاء وياء بعدها وباختلاس الكسرة وبسكون الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r5.speaker: مسلم بن جندب
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r5.claim: Muslim ibn Jundub reads the هاء with damma followed by wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن جندب بضم الهاء وواو بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r6.claim: Then turn away means withdraw; complete departure would conflict with the order to observe unless the sequence is inverted, as Ibn Zayd and Abu Ali propose, which the author finds unsuitable.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r6.anchor: لأن التولي بالكلية يينافي قوله : ( فانظر ماذا يرجعون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r7.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r7.claim: The order to stand back teaches proper etiquette with kings, as reported from Wahb.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r7.anchor: وأمره عليه السلام إياه بالتنحي من باب تعليم الآداب مع الملوك كما روي عن وهب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r8.claim: نظر means reflection; ماذا may be an interrogative object of the transitive verb يرجعون or the subject of a following clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r8.anchor: والنظر بمعنى التأمل والتفكر وماذاإما كلمة استفهام في موضع المفعول ليرجعون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r9.claim: A further parse makes ما an interrogative subject and ذا a relative predicate with an omitted resumptive; the clause is the object of a heart verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r9.anchor: وإما أن تكون ما استفهامية مبتدأ وذا اسم موصول بمعنى الذي خبره وجملة يرجعون صلة الموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r10.claim: Another view takes نظر as waiting, as in the cited verse; on this reading there is no suspended clause and ماذا is a relative object.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : النظر بمعنى الانتظار كما في قوله تعالى : ( أنظرونا نقتبس من نوركم ) فلا تعليق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r11.claim: The apparent sense is reflection and learning what the people say to one another in reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r11.anchor: والظاهر أنه بمعنى التأمل وأن المراد فتأمل وتعرف ماذا يرد بعضهم على بعض من القول

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r12.claim: The command implies that God gave the hoopoe the ability to understand what it heard.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r12.anchor: وهذا ظاهر في أن الله تعالى أعطى الهدهد قوة يفهم بها ما يسمعه من كلامهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r13.claim: The word ألقه is used because delivery requires the act of casting the letter.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r13.anchor: والتعبير بالقاء لأن تبليغه لايمكن بدونه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r14.claim: The plural pronoun shows that the letter was meant for the whole people.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p193#2/r14.anchor: وجمع الضمير لأن المقصود تبليغ ما فيه لجميع القوم والكشف عن حالهم بعده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158/r3.claim: After writing the letter, Solomon perfumed and sealed it with his ring, then told the hoopoe to deliver it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158/r3.anchor: فلما كتب الكتاب طبعه بالمسك وختمه بخاتمه. فقال للهدهد {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وقالون والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.claim: The readers differ on the hāʾ in “fa-alqih”: Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and Hamzah use sukūn; Abu Jaʿfar, Yaʿqub, and Qalun lightly pronounce kasra; others fully pronounce kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو، وعاصم، وحمزة: ساكنة الهاء، ويختلسها أبو جعفر، ويعقوب وقالون كسرا، [والآخرون بالإشباع كسرا]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.claim: “Then withdraw” means move away while remaining close to them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r2.anchor: {ثم تول عنهم} تنح عنهم فكن قريبا منهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r3.claim: “See what they return” means see what answer they give.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.claim: He reads the command with an advance and delay: deliver the letter, see their answer, then withdraw back to Solomon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p158#2/r4.anchor: في الآية تقديم وتأخير مجازها: اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون، ثم تول عنهم، أي: انصرف إلي،

BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r2.claim: Solomon orders the hoopoe to deliver the letter and withdraw to a nearby concealed place to observe what the recipients say to one another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:27:27-30/r2.anchor: ثم تنح عنهم إلى مكان قريب تتوارى فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r5.claim: Solomon immediately writes a very brief letter to remove the wrong of sun-worship quickly if the hoopoe's report is true, and gives it to the ready bird.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r5.anchor: فكتب له كتابا على الفورفي غاية الوجازة قصدا للإسراع في إزالة المنكر على تقدير صدق الهدهد بحسب الاستطاعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r6.claim: The فاء signals urgency: the bird flies as swiftly as lightning with God's added help, honoring His prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r6.anchor: أمده الله زيادة على ذلك بمعونة منه إكراما لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فصار كأنه البرق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r7.claim: Solomon addresses the letter to the whole group because they worship the sun, emphasizing the importance of religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p421#2/r7.anchor: أي الذين ذكرت أنهم يعبدون الشمس , وذلك للاهتمام بأمر الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r1.claim: After delivery, the hoopoe waits fluttering above them until they recognize the bearer, then withdraws to a safe place where it can hear their talk without being reached.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r1.anchor: أمره بأن يمكث بعد إلقائه يرفرف على رؤوسهم حتى يتحققوا أمره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r2.claim: Then marks the delay between delivery and withdrawal to let the recipients verify what happened.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p422/r2.anchor: فاشار سبحانه إلى ذلك بأداة التراخي بقوله , { ثم } أي بعد وصولك وإلقائك { تول }

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “then turn away” as staying close to them while awaiting their response.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اذهب بكتابي هذا} قال: كتب معه بكتاب فقال {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم} يقول: كن قريبا منهم

DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the hoopoe carried the letter to the middle of the queen’s throne, dropped it to her, and she read Solomon’s message.
DURR-FULL:v6p352/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اذهب بكتابي هذا} قال: كتب معه بكتاب فقال {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم}

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the hoopoe carried Solomon's letter in its beak, circled the queen's chamber, then dropped it to her; the letter included the basmala and a summons to submit.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : فذكر ما ذكر الله في كتابه فكتب سليمان الكتاب ، فاخذ بمنقاره

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Solomon sent the hoopoe with a letter, which it dropped onto the queen when it reached her throne.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس اصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين اذهب بكتابي هذا فالقه اليهم وكتب معه بكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the hoopoe carried the letter until it was level with the queen on her throne, then dropped it to her.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك قوله : اذهب بكتابي هذا فالقه اليهم فمضى الهدهد بالكتاب حتى اذا حاذى بالملكة وهي على عرشها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the queen as Balqis, daughter of Sharhabil of Yemen; after her people died she ruled, and the hoopoe slipped through a window and dropped the letter on her chest as she slept.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اذهب بكتابي هذا فالقه اليهم قال : ذكر لنا انها امراة من اهل اليمن كانت في بيت مملكة يقال لها بلقيس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r5.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r5.claim: Yazid ibn Ruman says the hoopoe carried the letter in its foot and dropped it through Balqis's window onto her lap after blocking the sun she worshipped; she was an astute, educated ruler from a royal house whose people followed Zoroastrianism.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2870#2/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، عن يزيد بن رومان اذهب بكتابي هذا فالقه اليهم ثم تول عنهم قال : فاخذ الهدهد الكتاب برجله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Solomon was to stay near the people and watch what they would say in response.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس ثم تول عنهم يقول : كن قريبا منهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r2.speaker: زهير بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r2.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad interprets the instruction as moving aside some distance from them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2871/r2.anchor: ثنا زهير بن محمد في قول الله : فالقه اليهم ثم تول عنهم يقول : تنح عنهم ناحية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r1.claim: The instruction to send the letter explains the preceding test of the hoopoe: the queen’s reply would verify its report, while silence would disprove it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r1.anchor: الجملة مبينة لجملة { سننظر أصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين } ( النمل : 27 ) لأن فيما سينكشف بعد توجيه كتابه إلى ملكة سبأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r2.claim: God inspired Solomon to contact Sheba by letter, bringing its kingdom within his influence, securing its resources and trade, and inviting its queen to submit and reform her people’s religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r2.anchor: ألهم الله سليمان بحكمته أن يجعل لاتصاله ببلاد اليمن طريق المراسلة لإدخال المملكة في حيز نفوذه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r3.claim: God gave Solomon’s rule such standing that neighboring kings feared him and sought his favor although his kingdom was smaller than Yemen and Egypt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r3.anchor: وليعلم أن الله ألقى في نفوس الملوك المعاصرين له رهبة من ملكه وجلبا لمرضاته لأن الله أيده وإن كانت مملكته أصغر من ممالك جيرانه مثل مملكة اليمن ومملكة مصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r4.claim: Solomon’s realm then extended around Jordan, Egypt’s frontier, and the Mediterranean.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r4.anchor: وكانت مملكة سليمان يومئذ محدودة بالأردن وتخوم مصر وبحر الروم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r5.claim: Exchanging letters was customary among states and preachers; the Prophet also wrote to Khosrow and Caesar, and Islamic governments prized official scribes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r5.anchor: ولم يزل تبادل الرسائل بين الملوك من سنة الدول ومن سنة الدعاة إلى الخير . وقد كتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى كسرى وقيصر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r6.claim: The hoopoe belongs to the pigeon family and can be domesticated; the command implies that Solomon prepared a letter and loaded it onto the bird.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r6.anchor: واتخذ للمراسلة وسيلة الطير الزاجل من حمام ونحوه ، فالهدهد من فصيلة الحمام وهو قابل للتدجين ، فقوله : { اذهب بكتابي هذا } يقتضي كلاما محذوفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r7.claim: The verb انظر is suspended from taking an object by the interrogative clause, and the author refers elsewhere for the analysis of ماذا.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r7.anchor: وتقدم القول على ( ماذا ) عند قوله تعالى : { وإذا قيل لهم ماذا أنزل ربكم } في سورة النحل ( 24 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r8.claim: إلقاء literally means casting to the ground; the letter could be dropped from the beak, or delivered figuratively by people taking it from the hoopoe’s leg.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r8.anchor: والإلقاء : الرمي إلى الأرض . وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { وألقوه في غيابات الجب } في سورة يوسف ( 10 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r9.claim: The figurative use of إلقاء is comparable to the verse in which people cast words to one another, if the letter was taken from the bird’s foot.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p256#2/r9.anchor: فيكون الإلقاء مثل قوله : { فألقوا إليهم القول إنكم لكاذبون في سورة النحل ( 86 )

FARRA:v2p291/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p291/r4.claim: The instruction to turn away and then see the reply is a semantic ordering: Solomon urges the hoopoe to hurry, then look at the response.
FARRA:v2p291/r4.anchor: ثم أخر (فانظر ماذا يرجعون) ومعناها التقديم.

FARRA:v2p291/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p291/r5.speaker: يقال
FARRA:v2p291/r5.claim: Another account says the hoopoe left the letter, hid from the queen, and watched from a window in her chamber.
FARRA:v2p291/r5.anchor: ففعل: ألقى الكتاب وطار إلى كوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r1.claim: The sequence “deliver it, then withdraw” with “observe” interposed leaves the matter to the letter’s contents, without escorting or pressing the recipients.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: واتساق رتبة الكلام أظهر أي «ألقه ثم تول» وفي خلال ذلك فانظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ reads the pronoun suffix in “fa-alqihi” with kasra; another group reads it with ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع «فألقه» بكسر الهاء، وفرقة «فألقه» بضمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r3.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن عامر، الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r3.claim: They lengthen with a yāʾ after the kasra; Warsh also transmits a yāʾ after the suffix in connected speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي بإشباع ياء بعد الكسرة في الهاء، وروى عنه ورش بياء بعد الهاء في الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r4.claim: Some lengthen with a wāw after the ḍamma; al-Bazzī from Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza reads the suffix with sukūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r4.anchor: وقرأ قوم بإشباع واو بعد الضمة، وقرأ البزي عن أبي عمرو وعاصم وحمزة «فألقه» بسكون الهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r5.claim: Wahb’s story says the Hudhud entered through the opening made for the rising sun and dropped the letter on the sleeping Queen; she woke startled, then saw the bird and summoned her court.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p257/r5.anchor: وروي عن وهب بن منبه في قصص هذه الآية أن الهدهد وصل فألفى دون هذه الملكة حجب جدرات فعمد إلى كوة كانت بلقيس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r1.claim: Solomon wrote and sealed a letter, then handed it to the hoopoe to deliver.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r1.anchor: ثم كتب كتابا وختمه بخاتمه ودفعه إلى الهدهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and al-Kisa'i read the final pronoun in فألقهي connected to a yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي فألقهي موصولة بياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم وأبو جعفر وحمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r3.claim: These readers recite فألقه with a silent hāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وعاصم وأبو جعفر وحمزة فألقه بسكون الهاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r4.speaker: قالون عن نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r4.claim: Qalun, transmitting from Nafi, reads the hāʾ with kasra and no lengthening.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r4.anchor: وروى قالون عن نافع كسر الهاء من غير إشباع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r5.claim: The letter is to the people of Sheba.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r6.claim: The command “then turn away from them” is explained either as turning aside or departing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r6.anchor: ثم تول عنهم فيه قولان أحدهما أعرض والثاني انصرف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r7.claim: “See what they return” means observe what answer they give.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r7.anchor: فانظر ماذا يرجعون أي ماذا يردون من الجواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r8.claim: Wahb says Solomon should withdraw unseen, then observe their answer from concealment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r8.anchor: أن المعنى ثم تول عنهم مستترا من حيث لا يرونك فانظر ماذا يردون من الجواب وهذا قول وهب بن منبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the wording as transposed: first see their response, then turn away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p167#2/r9.anchor: والثاني أن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا تقديره فانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم وهذا مذهب ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r2.claim: One report says the hoopoe carried Solomon's letter on its wing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r2.anchor: قيل: في جناحه كما هي عادة الطير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r3.claim: Another report says the hoopoe carried the letter in its beak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r4.claim: The hoopoe brought the letter to Bilqis's private chamber, dropped it before her through an opening, then withdrew courteously.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p188/r4.anchor: فألقاه إليها من كوة هنالك (4) بين يديها، ثم تولى ناحية أدبا ورياسة

NAHHAS:v3p208/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p208/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p208/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq lists five forms for ‘throw it to them’: retain the yāʾ, delete it but show its kasra, use a ḍamma with waw, delete the waw but show ḍamma, or—Ḥamza’s reading—make the hāʾ quiescent.
NAHHAS:v3p208/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق فيها خمسة أوجه ( فألقهي إليهم ) بإثبات الياء في اللفظ

NAHHAS:v3p208/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p208/r2.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p208/r2.claim: The grammarians only permit the quiescent-hāʾ reading by an artificial assumption of pausing; ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān says to disregard it, since the same logic would permit dropping case endings from nouns in connected speech.
NAHHAS:v3p208/r2.anchor: وهذا عند النحويين لا يجوز إلا على حيلة بعيدة يكون يقدر الوقف وسمعت علي ابن سليمان يقول لا تلتفت إلى هذه اللغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the hoopoe carried the letter in its beak, circled in the queen’s chamber, and dropped it to her after she remarked on the bird.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد أخذ الهدهد الكتاب بمنقاره فأتى بهوها فجعل يدور فيه فقالت ما رأيت خيرا منذ رأيت هذا الطير في بهوي فألقى الكتاب إليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r3.claim: Qatāda says the hoopoe dropped the letter onto the queen’s chest while she slept.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r3.anchor: قال قتادة : فألقاه على صدرها وهي نائمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r4.speaker: يزيد بن رومان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r4.claim: Yazīd ibn Rūmān says the queen had ruled after earlier members of her family and had been trained in governance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r4.anchor: قال يزيد بن رومان : كانت في ملك من مضى من أهلها وقد سيست وساست حتى أحكمها ذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “then withdraw from them” as staying close by.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p205/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس كن قريبا منهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā and al-Farrāʾ say the wording has delayed order: deliver the letter, watch their reply, and then withdraw.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p206/r1.anchor: فيه تقديم وتأخير تقديره فألقه إليهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم , حكاه ابن عيسى , وقاله الفراء

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r3.claim: Solomon sends his letter to the people of Sheba and tells the hoopoe to withdraw and watch what reply they make.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r3.anchor: وقال: { اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم } يعنى إلى أهل سبأ

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r4.claim: The hoopoe carries the letter in its beak, drops it into the queen’s lap, and its seal makes her and her troops tremble and submit; Solomon’s authority was in his seal.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r4.anchor: فحمل الهدهد الكتاب بمنقاره، فطار حتى وقف على رأس المرأة، فرفرف ساعة والناس ينظرون،

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r5.claim: The queen recognizes the messenger’s king as greater than her because a bird serves as his envoy.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r5.anchor: لأن ملك سليمان، عليه السلام، كان فى خاتمه فعرفوا أن الذى أرسل هذا الطير أعظم ملكا من ملكها،

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.claim: The queen was Arab, from the people of Tubbaʿ ibn Abi Sharahil al-Himyari, and her people were Arabs of Tubbaʿ’s people.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r6.anchor: وكانت عربية من قوم تبع بن أبى شراحيل الحميرى، وقومها من قوم تبع، وهم عرب،

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.claim: The letter contained only the statement that it was from Solomon, the basmala, a prohibition against exalting themselves over him, and a demand to come submitting.
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r7.anchor: فأخبرتهم بما فى الكتاب، ولم يكن فيه شىء غير: " إنه من سليمان، وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

MUQATIL:27:27-32/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
MUQATIL:27:27-32/r8.claim: Abu Salih reports that the letter was sealed.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r1.claim: Abu Amr, Asim, and Hamza read the final ه with sukūn; Yazid, Qalun, and Yaqub use a reduced kasra, while others retain the ya.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r1.anchor: بسكون الهاء تخفيفا أبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة ويختلسها كسر التدل الكسرة على الياء المحذوفة يزيد وقالون ويعقوب قالفهى باثبات الياء غيرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r2.claim: The addressees are Bilqis and her people, whom the hoopoe had mentioned together; therefore the letter uses a plural address.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r2.anchor: إلى بلقيس وقومها لأنه ذكرهم معها في قوله وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس وبني الخطاب في الكتاب على لفظ الجمع لذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r3.claim: Solomon tells the hoopoe to move to a nearby place where he can see them without being seen, so he can hear their response.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r3.anchor: تنح عنهم إلى مكان قريب بحيث تراهم ولا يرونك ليكون ما يقولونه بمسمع عنك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r4.claim: The hoopoe takes the letter in its beak, enters through a window, drops it on the sleeping queen’s chest, and hides; she wakes in fright.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r4.anchor: فاخذ الهدهد الكتاب بمنقاره ودخل عليها من كوة فطرح الكتاب على نحرها وهي راقدة وتوارى في الكوة فانتبهت فزعة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r5.claim: Alternatively, with soldiers around her, the hoopoe flutters and drops the letter in her lap; she can read.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p210#4/r5.anchor: أو أتاها الجنود حواليها فرفرف ساعة وألقى الكتاب في حجرها وكانت قارئة

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r1.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r1.claim: Maqatil says the hoopoe carried the letter in its beak, fluttered above the queen amid her troops, then dropped it into her lap.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r1.anchor: وقال مقاتل: حمل الهدهد الكتاب بمنقاره، وطار حتى وقف على رأس المرأة وحولها الجنود والعساكر، فرفرف ساعة والناس ينظرون إليه،

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r2.claim: The verse establishes sending letters to polytheists to convey the call and invite them to Islam; the Prophet wrote to Kisra, Caesar, and rulers.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r2.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على إرسال الكتب إلى المشركين وتبليغهم الدعوة، ودعائهم إلى الإسلام. وقد كتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى كسرى وقيصر وإلى كل جبار

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Solomon's instruction to turn away was courteous conduct with a monarch but meant to remain close enough to observe the reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r3.anchor: أمره بالتولي حسن أدب ليتنحى حسب ما يتأدب به مع الملوك. بمعنى: وكن قريبا حتى ترى مراجعتهم قاله وهب بن منبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes turning away to mean returning to Solomon after delivering the letter.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أمره بالتولي بمعنى الرجوع إليه أي ألقه وارجع.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the command to see their response as parenthetical and forward in sense: deliver, withdraw, and meanwhile wait for their reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r5.anchor: قال وقوله: { فانظر ماذا يرجعون } في معنى التقديم على قوله: { ثم تول } واتساق رتبة الكلام أظهر أي ألقه ثم تول، وفي خلال ذلك فانظر أي انتظر.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r6.claim: One gloss reads فانظر as know and interprets the command as asking what they will reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r6.anchor:
وقيل: فاعلم كقوله:
يوم ينظر المرء ما قدمت يداه [النبأ: 40] أي اعلم ماذا يرجعون أي يجيبون وماذا يردون من القول.

QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r7.claim: Another view takes the instruction as asking what they say among themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:27:28/r7.anchor: وقيل: { فانظر ماذا يرجعون } بينهم من الكلام.

RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r7.claim: The command to deliver it to them uses the plural because the hoopoe had found the queen and her people worshipping the sun, so the group is intended.

RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r8.claim: Turning away means withdrawing to a nearby concealed place so Solomon can hear their response; return is used in the sense of people answering one another, as in 34:30.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r8.anchor: و { يرجعون } من قوله تعالى : { يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول } ( سبأ : 30 )

RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r9.claim: It is also said that the hoopoe entered by an opening, dropped the letter to the queen, and concealed himself in that opening.
RAZI-FULL:v24p166/r9.anchor: ويقال دخل عليها من كوة وألقى إليها الكتاب وتوارى في الكوة

STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.claim: The account of Solomon's miraculous host and encounter with the Queen of Sheba ends with her embracing faith in the One God.
STUDYQURAN:27:intro/r5.anchor: Solomon with his miraculous host of men, jinn, and birds and his encounter with the Queen of Sheba, who eventually comes before Solomon

STUDYQURAN:27:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r1.claim: Solomon's words in these verses are addressed to the hoopoe.
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r1.anchor: Solomon is speaking to the hoopoe (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:27:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r2.claim: The hoopoe's categorical claim in 27:22 about knowing what Solomon did not know explains Solomon's test.
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r2.anchor: the hoopoe had made such a categorical claim in v. 22 regarding what he knew and what Solomon did not know (Q)

STUDYQURAN:27:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r3.claim: The passage shows that a leader should accept legitimate excuses from followers.
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r3.anchor: it also shows that a leader should accept the legitimate excuses of his followers (Q)

STUDYQURAN:27:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r4.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī cites a hadith saying God loves excuses most, which is why He revealed Books and sent messengers.
STUDYQURAN:27:27/r4.anchor: quotes a ḥadīth that states,“None love excuses more than God.

TAB-FULL:v18p45/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the sequence as deferred: the hoopoe watches the queen’s response after delivering the letter, then returns to Solomon; his report says it blocked her sun-facing window and dropped the letter before flying away.
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " فأجابه سليمان، يعني أجاب الهدهد لما فرغ: {قال سننظر أصدقت أم كنت من الكاذبين. اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم} [النمل: 28] وانظر ماذا يرجعون

TAB-FULL:v18p45/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r2.claim: Wahb says the hoopoe should stay near the recipients after delivering the letter and watch what they say in response.
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r2.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قوله: " {فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم} [النمل: 28] أي كن قريبا {فانظر ماذا يرجعون} [النمل: 28] "

TAB-FULL:v18p45/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers staying nearby because the queen consulted her people only after receiving the letter, and the hoopoe had to witness their discussion as ordered.
TAB-FULL:v18p45/r3.anchor: وهذا القول أشبه بتأويل الآية، لأن مراجعة المرأة قومها، كانت بعد أن ألقي إليها الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports that the hoopoe carried the letter until it was opposite the queen on her throne, then cast it to her.
TAB-FULL:v18p46/r4.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم}

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r1.claim: Hādhā may be an adjective of kitābī, an appositional substitute, or an explanatory apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r1.anchor: قوله: { هذا }: يجوز أن يكون صفة ل " كتابي " أو بدلا منه أو بيانا له.

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r2.claim: The common qirāʾāt vary the hāʾ of alqihi: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah, and Abū Bakr use sukūn; Qālūn has kasra without liaison; Hishām has both; the others use liaison.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر بإسكان الهاء، وقالون بكسرها فقط من غير صلة بلا خلاف عنه. وهشام عنه وجهان بالقصر والصلة. والباقون بالصلة بلا خلاف.

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r3.speaker: مسلم بن جندب
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r3.claim: Muslim ibn Jundub reads alqihū with a ḍamma and a connected wāw, noting that ḍamma is the original form.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r3.anchor: وقرأ مسلم بن جندب بضم الهاء موصولة بواو: " فألقهو إليهم " وقد تقدم أن الضم الأصل.

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r4.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī and others posit word order inversion, putting look at their response before turning away.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r4.anchor: زعم أبو علي وغيره أن في الكلام تقديما وأن الأصل: فانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم.

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r5.claim: The author says inversion is unnecessary: the meaning works as written, with Solomon staying nearby to see their response.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى هذا [لأن المعنى بدونه صحيح أي: قف قريبا منهم لتنظر ماذا يكون].

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r6.claim: If unẓur means consider, mādhā can be a single interrogative object of yarjiʿūn, or mā can be interrogative with dhā as a relative; in either analysis the question is suspended as the object of unẓur.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r6.anchor: إن جعلنا " انظر " بمعنى تأمل وتفكر كانت " ما " استفهامية. وفيها حينئذ وجهان،/ أحدهما: أن تجعل مع " ذا " بمنزلة اسم واحد

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r7.claim: If unẓur means wait, mādhā is a relative meaning what they return, directly governed as the object of wait.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r7.anchor: وإن جعلناه بمعنى انتظر من قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r8.claim: The Shaykh likewise distinguishes an interrogative mādhā from mā plus a relative dhā, with yarjiʿūn as either predicate or relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28/r8.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " وماذا: إن كان معنى " انظر " معنى التأمل بالفكر كان " انظر " معلقا.

SAMIN-DURR:27:28#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:27:28#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:27:28#2/r1.claim: The author rejects the Shaykh's first parse: if all of mādhā is the interrogative object of yarjiʿūn, that verb cannot also be its predicate; it governs the interrogative while the whole clause is suspended under unẓur.
SAMIN-DURR:27:28#2/r1.anchor: كيف يكون خبرا عنه وهو منصوب به كما تقدم تقريره؟

TABATABAI:27:26-30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r4.claim: Solomon's command to take the letter is addressed to the hoopoe and names the Queen of Sheba and her council as its recipients; the bird is then to watch what answer they exchange.
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r4.anchor: فكتب سليمان كتابا ثم قال للهدهد اذهب بكتابي هذا إليهم أي إلى ملكة سبأ وملأها

TABATABAI:27:26-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r5.claim: The verb phrase directing the hoopoe to deliver the letter has a vowelless ha in every recitation, whether connected or paused, which is the ha of pause.
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r5.anchor: وقوله { فألقه } بسكون الهاء وصلا ووقفا في جميع القراءات وهي هاء السكت

TABATABAI:27:26-30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r6.claim: The proposed precedence and delay that moves watching before withdrawal is, in the author's view, untenable.
TABATABAI:27:26-30/r6.anchor: من قبيل التقديم والتأخير والأصل فانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم. وهو كما ترى

TABRISI:27:27-31/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r4.claim: Solomon wrote the letter, sealed it with his ring, and gave it to the hoopoe to deliver.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r4.anchor: ثم كتب سليمان كتابا وختمه بخاتمه ودفعه إليه فذلك قوله { اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم

TABRISI:27:27-31/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r5.claim: The letter was addressed to the people of Sheba.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r5.anchor: يعني إلى أهل سبأ { ثم تول عنهم }

TABRISI:27:27-31/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه وغيره
TABRISI:27:27-31/r6.claim: After dropping the letter, the hoopoe hid close by and watched what response they gave.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r6.anchor: أي أستتر منهم قريبا بعد إلقاء الكتاب إليهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون عن وهب بن منبه وغيره.

TABRISI:27:27-31/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:27:27-31/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:27:27-31/r7.claim: Some reverse the order, having the hoopoe watch the reply before withdrawing; the author prefers the plain order because the wording works without rearrangement.
TABRISI:27:27-31/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنه على التقديم والتأخير { فانظر ماذا يرجعون } أي ماذا يردون من الجواب ثم تول عنهم

THALABI:v7p204#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p204#3/r5.claim: Solomon told the hoopoe to deliver the letter, withdraw while remaining nearby, and observe what answer they returned.
THALABI:v7p204#3/r5.anchor: فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم فكن قريبا منهم فانظر ماذا يرجعون يردون من الجواب

THALABI:v7p204#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p204#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v7p204#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the order as delivery, then observing their reply, then withdrawing; “turn away” has the same sense as in another verse.
THALABI:v7p204#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: في الآية تقديم وتأخير مجازها: اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم وانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم أي انصرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p216#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p216#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p216#2/r1.claim: Solomon wrote and sealed a letter, handed it to the hoopoe, and sent it to the people of Sheba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p216#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: كتب سليمان كتابا وختمه بخاتمه، ودفعه إلى الهدهد، وقال له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r1.claim: He glosses the command to turn away as withdrawing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r1.anchor: قوله: {ثم تول عنهم} قال مقاتل: انصرف عنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r2.claim: Another gloss is to turn away or show disregard.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: انصرف عنهم (¬1). وقيل: أعرض عنهم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the sequence as fronted and delayed: deliver the letter, see their response, then withdraw, since withdrawal follows receiving their answer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد: هذا على التأخير والتقديم، المعنى: اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم، فانظر ماذا يرجعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj approves Ibn Zayd's reordered sequence, noting that fronting and delaying are common in speech.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا حسن، والتقديم والتأخير كثير في الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r5.claim: Without rearranging the order, the command means to hide where they cannot see the hoopoe and observe their reply.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r5.anchor: ومن لم يحمل الآية على التقديم والتأخير قال: معناه: {ثم تول عنهم} مستترا من حيث لا يرونك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r6.claim: The hoopoe is said to have dropped the letter and hidden in a window opening in the queen's chamber.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p219/r6.anchor: فيقال: إن الهدهد فعل ذلك: ألقى الكتاب وطار إلى كوة (¬6) في مجلسها متواريا # عنها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r1.claim: Solomon tells the hoopoe to step back a short distance and watch what answer the queen sends; the hoopoe delivers the letter to her.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:27:28-34/r1.anchor: أي: استأخر غير بعيد { فانظر ماذا يرجعون } ما يردون من الجواب، فمضى الهدهد، وألقى إليها الكتاب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r1.claim: Solomon tells the hoopoe to leave after delivering the letter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {اذهب بكتابي هذا فألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم} [النمل: 28] يقول: ثم انصرف عنهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.claim: Qatāda relates that Bilqīs, daughter of Sharāḥbīl, was a Yemeni woman from a royal household; after her people died, she became their ruler.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r2.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: ذكر لنا أنها امرأة من أهل اليمن كانت في بيت مملكة، يقال لها بلقيس ابنة شرحبيل، فهلك قومها، فملكت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.claim: Abū Bakra reports that the Prophet said a people ruled by a woman will not prosper.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r3.anchor: وحدثني المبارك، عن الحسن، عن أبي بكرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لن يفلح قوم تملكهم امرأة» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.claim: Qatāda says Bilqīs locked the doors, put the keys under her head, and went to bed; the hoopoe entered through an opening and dropped the letter on her belly or between her breasts, where she found it and read it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p541/r4.anchor: سعيد، قال قتادة: وأنها كانت إذا رقدت غلقت الأبواب، وأخذت المفاتيح فوضعتها تحت رأسها، فلما غلقت الأبواب وآوت إلى فراشها أتاها الهدهد حتى دخل من كوة بيتها، فقذف الصحيفة على بطنها أو بين ثدييها، فأخذت الصحيفة فقرأتها

BURHAN:v3p292/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p292/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p292/r1.claim: The order of the conjuncts is reversed: Solomon should observe their response before turning away, since observing is impossible once he has withdrawn.
BURHAN:v3p292/r1.anchor: حقيقته فانظر ماذا يرجعون ثم تول عنهم لأنه نظره ما يرجعون من القول غير متأت مع توليه

BURHAN:v3p292/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p292/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p292/r2.claim: Taking turning away as hiding in the niche from which he delivered the letter is figurative; the literal reading is preferable.
BURHAN:v3p292/r2.anchor: وما يفسر به التولي من أنه يتوارى في الكوة التي ألقى منها الكتاب مجاز والحقيقة راجحة عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī used poetry in his sermons, including a verse contrasting a woman’s present charm with the next man’s embrace.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r1.anchor: وكان الحسن البصري ، رحمه الله ، يتمثل في مواعظه بالأبيات من الشعر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r2.claim: Al-Marzubānī preserves a report from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr about ʿUmar distributing Yemeni garments: he rejected Zayd’s preferential choice, then hid the garments and let each man draw one; the narrator calls this exceptionally fair.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه - ذكره المرزباني في كتابه بإسناد عن عبد الملك بن عمير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r3.claim: The text identifies ʿUmāra ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and recounts how a woman asked him to stop drinking; after swearing off wine, he later hosted drinkers, slaughtered his camel, and had to answer her in verse.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r3.anchor: وعمارة هذا هو عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة ، خطب امرأة من قومه فقالت : لا أتزوجك أو تترك الشراب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r4.claim: A joking or otherwise false utterance can serve a serious purpose: poetry may be used to establish a truth or as an example for a noble end, as in the example attributed to Abū Tammām.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p29/r4.anchor: فإذا رب ، هزل أداة في جد ، وكلام جرى في باطل ، ثم استعين به على حق

DAMGHANI:v1p498/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r4.claim: Tawallā can mean departing or withdrawing from people.
DAMGHANI:v1p498/r4.anchor: فوجه منها تولى بمعنى انصرف قوله تعالى في سورة النمل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r1.claim: The verb تولى can mean holding authority, as when someone becomes a governor over others.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r1.anchor: التولي يقال ، ويراد به الولاية . يقال : تولى فلان علينا ، أي : صار واليا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r2.claim: The verb can also mean turning away from someone.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r2.anchor: ويقال ] ، ويراد : به الإعراض . يقال : تولى فلان عنا إذا أعرض .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r3.claim: One Qur'anic use is departure or turning aside, illustrated by those who turn away, Solomon's instruction, and Moses' going to the shade.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p214/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن التولي في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.claim: He calls this fā the explicative fā that signals omitted but understood events, as in the unspoken striking of the stone, the steps after the command to go, and the Hudhud’s delivery of Solomon’s letter.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p94/r4.anchor: هذه الفاء إذن هي فاء الفصيحة التي تدلّ على أن هناك محذوف ولكن المعنى واضح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.claim: In Solomon’s story, the text omits the hoopoe taking the letter, carrying and dropping it by Bilqis, and waiting; the meaning remains clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p544/r4.anchor: المفروض أن الهدهد أخذ الكتاب وذهب به وألقاه عند بلقيس وانتظر

NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.claim: Twelve letters in twenty places depart from the regular rules; examples include fa-alqihi ilayhim and an lam yarahu.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.anchor: وعدته اثنا عشر حرفا في عشرين موضعا

NASHR:v2p337/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p337/r8.claim: The reading of فألقه was treated earlier under the rules for the pronominal hāʾ.
NASHR:v2p337/r8.anchor: وتقدم فألقه في باب هاء الكناية

NASHR:v1p305/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p305/r6.speaker: حفص وعاصم
NASHR:v1p305/r6.claim: The same disagreement applies to the hāʾ of فألقه إليهم; Hafs makes it still, so all of Asim reads it with sukūn. The author also notes route-specific Abu Jafar readings.
NASHR:v1p305/r6.anchor: وكذا اختلافهم في فألقه إليهم، إلا أن حفصا سكن الهاء مع من أسكن

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r4.claim: He lists five forms of the command, including retaining or dropping yāʾ, retaining or dropping wāw, and a still hāʾ; retaining yāʾ is the commonest and strongest reading.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r4.anchor: ألقه إليهم ثم تول عنهم) - خمسة أوجه: فالقهي إليهم بإثبات الياء - وهو أكثر القراءة،

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r5.claim: The underlying form is فألقيه; the yāʾ deleted by the jussive can disappear before the pronoun hāʾ, explaining the preferred form.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r5.anchor: فإن الياء التي تسقط للجزم قد سقطت قبل الهاء، لأن الأصل فألقيه إليهم،

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r6.claim: Deleting the yāʾ while keeping kasra after hāʾ follows the preference to drop the yāʾ after hāʾ in ألقيه.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r6.anchor: ومن حذف الياء وترك الكسرة بعد الهاء فلأنه كان إذا أثبت الياء في قولك أنا ألقيه إليهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r7.claim: The waw form restores the original connected pronoun ending, as in ألقيتهو; when paused or written, it is represented by hāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ (فألقهو إليهم) رده إلى أصله، والأصل إثبات الواو مع هاء الإضمار. تقول ألقيتهو إليك.

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r8.claim: Dropping wāw while retaining ḍamma parallels dropping yāʾ while retaining kasra.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ بحذف الواو وإثبات الضمة فذلك مثل حذف الياء وإثبات الكسرة،

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r9.claim: He calls the still hāʾ reading mistaken: the pronoun is not jussive, although poetry can omit it and retain the preceding kasra.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r9.anchor: ومن أسكن الهاء فغالط، لأن لهاء ليست بمجزومة ولها وجه من القياس،

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r10.claim: He refers readers to his fuller explanation of the same pronoun construction in 4:75.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r10.anchor: وقد شرحنا ذلك في قوله (يؤده إليك) شرحا كافيا.

ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r11.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r11.claim: An unnamed poet's line preserves the preceding kasra when hāʾ is omitted, illustrating the poetic parallel.
ZAJJAJ:v4p116/r11.anchor: قال الشاعر: فإن يك غثا أوسمينا فإنني. . . سأجعل عينيه لنفسه مقنعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r13.claim: Solomon postponed judgment on the hoopoe until he could distinguish truth from falsehood, then wrote a letter for delivery.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r13.anchor: ثم إن سليمان عليه السلام أخر أمر الهدهد إلى أن يبين له حقه من باطله فسوفه بالنظر في ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r14.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r14.claim: Wahb says the hoopoe withdrew with courtly etiquette but stayed close enough to observe the rulers' reply.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r14.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه أمره بالتولي حسن أدب، ليتنحى حسبما يتأدب به مع الملوك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r15.claim: Ibn Zayd reads تول as return to Solomon after dropping the letter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r15.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أمره بالتولي بمعنى الرجوع إليه أي ألقه وارجع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r16.claim: Ibn Zayd says فانظر ماذا يرجعون is logically advanced before ثم تول.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p256#2/r16.anchor: قال وقوله فانظر ماذا يرجعون في معنى التقديم على قوله ثم تول
